signals.name: v1TreeVisits
signals.quantity: tree-bin nodes visited (one per read of TreeNode.hash) inside HashMap$TreeNode.find while QuicheQuicCodec.getChannel is on the stack
signals.storage: public static long DoSCounters.v1TreeVisits (bootstrap-loaded), gated by static int DoSCounters.v1Scope and the owner thread

signals.name: v1MaxPerLookup
signals.quantity: largest number of tree-bin nodes visited during a single getChannel call
signals.storage: public static long DoSCounters.v1MaxPerLookup, updated at getChannel exit from a per-call delta

signals.name: v1KeyEquals
signals.quantity: ByteBuffer.equals key comparisons inside getChannel (covers list bins before treeification)

signals.name: channelsAdded
signals.quantity: number of QuicheQuicCodec.addChannel invocations (distinct connections whose DCID entered the map)

plans.retention: Keep the input if v1TreeVisits, v1MaxPerLookup, v1KeyEquals or channelsAdded reaches a new maximum, or (flat-signal criterion) if it is longer than every kept input at the same log2 level of v1TreeVisits while that level's longest is below input_bytes=413000. Scheduling: with probability 0.30, while the longest kept input is below input_bytes, apply flat growth to it (append fresh records until it doubles, cut at input_bytes). With probability 0.10 (0.25 once input_bytes is reached), apply dense growth to the highest-scoring input (hash-preserving carry clone of every record, x2; x1.25 above input_bytes; up to MAX_INPUT_SIZE). Otherwise mutate a parent chosen by rank (v1TreeVisits, then v1MaxPerLookup), with growth bounded by max(parent length, input_bytes). Fresh records prefer 20-byte DCIDs. Corpus in out/V1/corpus, metadata in out/V1/meta.
mutation: record-level replace/insert/splice/length, using the harness's [len][dcid] parse
repetition: repeat a run of records k times (k up to doubling the input) and double the whole input
flat growth: append fresh records until the input doubles, toward input_bytes

dense growth / clone with hash-preserving carry: per-record (+31,-1)/(-31,+1) adjacent-byte adjustments derived from the ByteBuffer.hashCode base-31 polynomial, applied to whatever records the search selected
dictionary tokens from the attack path: 20 (Quic.MAX_CONN_ID_LEN), 8, 10, 0, 31, 0x7f, 0x80, 0xff, 1
no encoder needed: the harness applies the QUIC Initial protection

signals.name: p1TreeVisits
signals.quantity: tree-bin nodes visited inside HashMap$TreeNode.find while HashMap$TreeNode.putTreeVal runs within QuicheQuicCodec.addChannel
signals.storage: public static long DoSCounters.p1TreeVisits, gated by DoSCounters.addScope and DoSCounters.putScope and the owner thread

signals.name: p1VisitsPerKB
signals.quantity: p1TreeVisits divided by the KB of datagram content received by QuicheQuicCodec.channelRead in the same execution (both measured)
signals.storage: DoSCounters.p1TreeVisits and DoSCounters.datagramBytes (incremented at channelRead entry by msg.content().readableBytes()); ratio computed in PkgRisk1Guidance.handleResult()

signals.name: p1Treeify
signals.quantity: HashMap$TreeNode.treeify invocations within addChannel (a colliding bin crossed TREEIFY_THRESHOLD)

signals.name: p1KeyEquals
signals.quantity: ByteBuffer.equals key comparisons during insertion inside addChannel (list bins before treeification)

plans.retention: Keep the input if p1TreeVisits, p1VisitsPerKB, p1Treeify, p1KeyEquals or channelsAdded reaches a new maximum, or (flat-signal criterion) if it is longer than every kept input at the same log2 level of p1TreeVisits while that level's longest is below input_bytes=176000. Scheduling: with probability 0.30, while the longest kept input is below input_bytes, apply flat growth to it (append fresh records until it doubles, cut at input_bytes). With probability 0.10 (0.25 once input_bytes is reached), apply dense growth to the highest-scoring input (hash-preserving carry clone of every record, x2; x1.25 above input_bytes; up to MAX_INPUT_SIZE). Otherwise mutate a parent chosen by rank (p1TreeVisits, then p1VisitsPerKB), with growth bounded by max(parent length, input_bytes). Fresh records prefer 8-10 byte DCIDs (densest encoding), plus a record-shortening operator. Corpus in out/PkgRisk1/corpus, metadata in out/PkgRisk1/meta.
